sentences.text: Megacephalosaurus is named for its massive head, which is the largest known among all plesiosaurs found in North America.
The holotype skull, the specimen the species is based on, measures 150 centimeters in cranium length and 171 centimeters in lower jaw length.
A second specimen, the paratype, is estimated to have had a complete skull length of 175 centimeters, making it larger than the holotype.
Based on these skull dimensions, the animal likely reached a total body length between 6 and 9 meters.
Its skull holds the record for the largest known plesiosaur skull from the North American continent.
The teeth were somewhat circular in shape and featured ridges designed to improve gripping and puncturing prey.
The genus was formally described by Schumacher and colleagues in 2013.
The first fossils were discovered in 1950.
The initial specimen was found on June 5, 1950, by teenage brothers Frank and Robert Jennrich while they were collecting fossil shark teeth near Fairport, Kansas.
In November 2003, Robert Jennrich returned to lead museum staff back to the original site to re-examine the locality.
Currently, only two fossil specimens of this animal are known to science.
Its long snout and uniform-sized teeth suggest it fed on smaller-sized prey.
Researchers propose that apicobasal ridges on the teeth helped improve gripping and puncturing prey.
The subfamily Brachaucheninae, to which Megacephalosaurus belongs, is currently known only from the Cretaceous period.
A defining characteristic of Brachaucheninae members like Megacephalosaurus is the possession of somewhat circularly-shaped teeth.
The type species of the genus is Megacephalosaurus eulerti.
Brachauchenius lucasi and Brachauchenius eulerti are considered synonyms of Megacephalosaurus.
The animal belongs to the subfamily Brachaucheninae.
The genus is classified within the family Pliosauridae.
Megacephalosaurus lived approximately 93.9 to 92.9 million years ago during the Turonian stage.
Fossils have been found in what is now North America, where the animal inhabited the Western Interior Seaway in the middle of the continent.
The holotype was found in the Fairport Chalk member of the Carlile Shale, dated to approximately 92.9 million years ago.
The temporal range of Megacephalosaurus extended past the Cenomanian-Turonian boundary and the subsequent anoxic event.
Recent discoveries challenge the hypothesis that Megacephalosaurus was the only pliosaur lineage to cross the Jurassic-Cretaceous boundary.
It is debated whether additional fossils currently identified as Brachauchenius lucasi actually belong to Megacephalosaurus.
